items.title: Agentic AI turns simple language into self-guided X-ray scans of microelectronics
items.excerpt: Science has increasingly used artificial intelligence (AI) as a kind of microscope—sorting data, analyzing images and revealing hidden patterns. Now a new shift is underway: AI that not only breaks down data but also helps scientists decide what to do next through simple, natural
items.rationale: An AI agent takes plain-language instructions and steers X-ray imaging of microelectronics on its own. This moves AI from analyzing data to running the instrument, and it is a different instrument and study from the 09-15 AFM microscope card.

items.title: AI techniques behind image creation improve flash flood forecasts across U.S. river basins
items.excerpt: A flash flood can devastate a community for years in a matter of minutes. These disasters account for roughly 85% of floods and cause thousands of deaths annually worldwide, with water levels capable of shooting up 30 feet (9 meters) and receding to normal levels in the span of a
items.rationale: A specific new hydrology result that applies image-generation methods to flash-flood forecasting across U.S. river basins. The history_match (09-13) is a general feature on AI disaster forecasting, not this study.

items.title: AI may help catch heart transplant rejection without biopsies
items.excerpt: By analyzing heart rhythm recordings and blood tests, artificial intelligence may accurately flag when a transplant patient's body starts attacking a donated heart, a new study suggests.
items.rationale: New clinical study in which AI reads ECGs and blood tests to flag heart transplant rejection without invasive biopsies. It is a different condition and study from the 09-12 STAT heart-attack EKG card and the 09-30 xECG card.

items.title: Unlocking Earth AI's planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health
items.excerpt: Google Research blog post on applying Earth AI's planetary geospatial foundation models to global public health (excerpt not extractable; enrichment pass should read the body).
items.rationale: Primary-source research release that applies geospatial foundation models to population-health questions. It adds a lab-blog outlet and an Earth-observation-meets-epidemiology field. The history_match (ocean sediment carbon, 09-09) is unrelated.

items.title: From food to fuel, AI helps pinpoint how to grow 'microalgae' at scale
items.excerpt: Microalgae (microscopic organisms that use light and carbon dioxide to grow) can be used to make ingredients and food for animals, pigments and potentially renewable fuels. But growing microalgae efficiently at an industrial scale is difficult.
items.rationale: Applied bioprocess result in which AI finds growth conditions for industrial-scale microalgae. It is fresh, has no counterpart in the 30-day history, and adds a biotech and energy field.
